key_insight: The paper shows that quantum machine learning can, in principle, be implemented blind and still retain computational advantages by compiling circuits into efficient brickwork graph states.
engineering_relevance: MasonQ provides a practical circuit-to-brickwork transpilation path for estimating depth, width, and qubit requirements of privacy-preserving quantum ML on near-term hardware.
method: Built MasonQ, a universal transpiler from arbitrary quantum circuits to computational brickwork graph states.
Derived asymptotic depth bound for UBQC brickwork graphs: D = O(ωn), with ω as circuit width and n as gate complexity.
Applied the framework to QFT, HHL, recommendation systems, and quantum transformers, including a 12-qubit minimal demo estimate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports new theoretical upper bounds, optimality claims up to logarithmic corrections, and concrete resource estimates derived from representative benchmark algorithms.
watch_item: The results are primarily asymptotic and theoretical, so real hardware overheads, noise, and compilation constants may materially affect practical performance.
paper_title: On the Computational Complexity of Blind Quantum Machine Learning
